study_identification_part.si4_title: Molecular and micro-architectural mapping of gray matter alterations in psychosis

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Characterize molecular and micro-architectural attributes that underlie cortical volume deviations across psychosis-related groups using centile-based normative modeling; map deviations to 46 neurobiological features to test regional vulnerability hypotheses.

rci2_hc_n.reason: The paper explicitly states in the Results section that centiles were computed for 38,696 healthy controls (HC). This is also mentioned in the Subjects section where it states 'Healthy controls (n = 38,232)' and then adds additional HC from PAFIP (n=195) and ALSPAC (n=269), totaling 38,696.
rci2_hc_n.supporting_text: Thus, after averaging brain volumes across hemispheres for each of the 34 Desikan-Killiany regions, centiles were computed for 38,696 HC and 1256 individuals classified under eight different psychosis-related diagnoses

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: A centile-based normative modeling approach (GAMLSS from brainchart/Lifespan) was used, which models and removes site effects. Specifically, study-specific offsets (random effects) for mean, variance, and skewness are estimated to align new data with the normative trajectory, accounting for batch effects.
rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: Using a centile method that removes age-, sex-, and site-effects [40], we were able to detect brain volume deviations from the expected trajectories. ... our out-of-sample data is aligned to the corresponding epoch of the normative trajectory, using maximum likelihood to estimate the study specific offsets (random effects) for three moments of the underlying statistical distributions: mean (μ), variance (σ), and skewness (ν) in an age- and sex-specific manner. This allows to compute centiles for each scan in a new study, on the same scale as the reference population curve, while accounting for study-specific ‘batch effects’.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: All psychosis-related groups show reduced cortical GM centiles below normative trajectories, strongest and most widespread in FEP and chronic SCZ/SAD; neurobiological features, especially metabolism and neurotransmitter receptors, co-localize with regions showing greatest deviations.
